Title: AKU-ACER November 2025 Highlights
NewsSummary: This month was packed with new grants, international collaborations, and policy influence
NewsContent:
November was a month of high achievement and significant momentum for the Aga Khan University's Arusha Climate and Environmental Research Centre (AKU-ACER). The Centre strengthened its global partnerships, secured major new funding, and deepened its influence on crucial policy discussions across Africa.

The month began with an important research exchange, as AKU-ACER hosted collaborators from the Bonn International Centre for Conflict Studies (BICC) in Germany. This visit facilitated key discussions on implementing their recently funded research project focused on carbon and environmental sustainability, laying the groundwork for future collaboration.

Looking ahead, the Centre successfully secured two major new grants that will fuel ambitious research for years to come. The first is the highly competitive Future Rural Africa Collaborative Research Centre (CRC), a multi-year project partnered with the Universities of Cologne and Bonn. The second grant, from the Climate Justice Resilience Fund, will support a critical initiative on Strengthening Pastoralist Resilience in the Mara-Serengeti Cluster (SPRM), directly addressing the impact of climate change on vulnerable communities.

AKU-ACER's expertise also reached high-level policy arenas. The Centre's Director Professor Emmanuel Sulle, played a key role on the scientific committee for the 6th Conference on Land Policy in Africa, co-organized by the African Union and UN agencies. A major contribution was the push for a Call to Action to integrate climate and environmental content into university curricula across the continent. This impact was further amplified when his conference blog was reposted by UNECA and other prominent continental institutions, boosting AKU-ACER's visibility.

The Centre celebrated its researchers at the AKU Authors' Day in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. Dr Bashir Adelodun received the prestigious Outstanding Research Impact Citation (2021-2025) and served as a panellist, providing insight into the evolving relationship between Artificial Intelligence (AI) and authorship. Our IT and Admin support technician, Kelvin Mwatusi was also in attendance.

On the publications front, AKU-ACER achieved a major milestone: publishing the first journal article using data generated at AKU land, focusing on accessible drone imaging for sustainable crop management. This, along with another article on long-term climate variability, underscores ACER's commitment to generating cutting-edge scientific knowledge for a sustainable future.
